newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW - RAKVERE READY FOR PORK IMPORT TARIFFS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - RAKVERE READY FOR PORK IMPORT TARIFFS.

text.p: Estonia's largest meat processor Rakvere still maintains its opposition to possible pork import tariffs but said it was ready to meet the issue by producing its own pork.
"The proposed tariffs are not good and will increase prices for consumers," finance director Teet Soorm told Reuters in an interview.
But he said the company was ready for any changes.
"The pig farm we bought last year will cover our present needs and if production increases we can buy more pig farms," Soorm added.
Rakvere is the largest meat processor in Estonia and has about 40-45 percent of the Estonian market.
It is looking for output of 80 tonnes of meat products a day in the summer and expects to reach 100 tonnes per day in 1998.
It also plans to open a representative office in Riga.
However, although most of the raw material is sourced locally, large amounts were imported in 1996.
During 1996, 20 to 30 percent of the raw product used by Rakvere was imported from the U.S. and Denmark.
"We imported frozen beef and pork carcasses last year, as well as frozen pork blocks," Soorm said.

Soorm said imported pork was cheaper than local pork but added that local producers are already making a profit and that the company takes this into account when dealing with demands for higher prices by local producers.
Despite the government's decision in principle to apply tariffs, Rakvere still does not know how much will be added to the cost of imported pork.
"The government has not said what is in store and so we cannot calculate the cost as yet," he said.
Tariffs are seen as part of a revived rural lobby and meat processors have been waging a campaign against it.
However, Rakvere expects demand for pork and products to remain stable and is seeking to expand its production into 1998.
Rakvere is the most modern meat processor in Estonia and moved to a new site and established new lines in 1991.
